Introduction

In this report we analyse the relationship between profit, revenue, economic sector and employees of companies to predict future market value of the company. The data used was collected from the Fortune magazine list of largest American companies by revenue. According to Fortune Wiki, as of 2020, the list top 500 companies make around 2/3 of the United Stated GDP with approximately $14.2 trillion in revenue, $1.2 trillion in profits and $20.4 in total market value, and its revenues account for approximately 18% of the gross world product.Therefore, those companies make a crucial impact on the economy and exploring the relationship between the companies corresponding financial metrics is important to make relevant predictions. For the purposes of this analysis, we have conducted appropriate data wrangling. A linear model was used to analyse the data to explore those relationships. This analysis was limited to using a linear regression of economic sector, profits, assets and revenue as predictors to model the market value. It is likely possible to improve the model further using more predictors available in the dataset.

Method

The data on financial metrics was collected by the Fortune magazine, listing the largest by revenue top 1000 companies in 2023 and top 500 companies in 2024. In our analysis we have chosen data for different years to be able to explore the financial metrics in dynamics. The fortune 2023 data contains 1000 observations of 31 variables. The fortune 2024 data contains 500 observations of 16 variables. In this analysis we will consider 14 variables:

  • Company: Company Name
  • State: The state in which the company headquarters is located.
  • MarketCap: Market capitalization in dollars, share value multiplied by number of shares.
  • Revenue: The revenue generated by the company in millions of dollars.
  • Assets: The assets of the company in millions of dollars.
  • Employees: The number of people employed by the company.
  • FounderCEO: Is the founder of the company the CEO, boolean true or false.
  • FemaleCEO: Is the CEO a woman, boolean true or false.
  • Profits: The profit of the company in millions of dollars.
  • Date: The end of the fiscal year, namely March 31 and corresponding year.
  • RevenueEmployee: Revenue divided by the number of employees.
  • ProfitMargin: Profit divided by Revenue.
  • EconomicSector: Industrial sectors grouped into 4 economic sectors, labeled by numbers:

  1. primary: is all companies whose IndustrialSector is Materials, Energy;

  2. secondary: is all companies whose IndustrialSector is Motor Vehicles & Parts, Food, Beverages & Tobacco, Household Products, Industrials, Aerospace & Defense, Chemicals, Apparel, Engineering & Construction.

  3. tertiary: is all companies whose IndustrialSector is Retailing, Health Care, Financials, Telecommunications, Food & Drug Stores, Transportation, Media, Hotels, Restaurants & Leisure, Wholesalers.

  4. quaternary: is all companies whose IndustrialSector is Technology, Business Services.

  • Year: Year when the data was collected.


Data Wrangling

Fortune 2024 dataset

The data was processed to clean it for the downstream analysis. In particular, the following operations were made:

  • Selected and renamed 14 variables for data readability and relevancy for the analysis.
  • Formatted numeric and boolean variables for data wrangling, exploration and modelling consistency.
  • Grouped values of Industrial sector variable into four Economic sectors labeled by numbers 1-4 for more convenient data classification and comparisons.
  • Created two new variables as ratios of profits, revenue and number of employees.

Data visual exploration

We have visually explored the relationships between market value, revenue, profits, CEO and economic sector for both fortune 2023 and 2024 datasets. Each visualisation shows the comparison between both years and provides insights on the variables and their dynamics.

As shown in Figure 1. below, there is clearly a right-skewed distribution for both years with majority of companies placed at the lower end on the scale. We can note a few outliers at the right tail - those are the companies generating highest amount of revenues.

Next, we have explored the proportion of female CEOs between both years. Would be worth exploring this variable in dynamics within a decade, but as for now the number of CEO females comparing to CEO males remains low.

Further, we have explored the association between the Profits as an assumed predictor and MarketCap - the market value estimation variable.

As can be seen in Figure 4, there is a positive correlation and linear relationship between both variables, suggesting that levels of profits are associated with market value. The trend line suggesting linear relationship is consistent across both years. The spread around the trend line indicates higher variability and can be an indicator of other factors that have association with market value. In 2024, some companies have visibly higher profits and market value, suggesting a possible growth or increase in profits for those companies.

Next, we have explored how the number of people companies employ varies across different economic sectors. As seen in Figure 5, overall the number of employees slightly increased in 2024 in comparison to 2023. Namely, number of employees in sector one (primary) increased by nearly 4 %, in sector three (tertiary) increased by only 1 % and sector four (quaternary) increased the most by 7,5 %. Only sector two (secondary) had a slight decrease by 0.6 %. Increase in employment in the quaternary sector can indicate financial growth on that economic sector.

Statistical modelling

We fitted a linear model to predict the market value of the company using the variables economic sector, profits, assets and revenue as predictors. We fitted a linear model of natural log of MarketCap as the response variable. We fitted a natural log for the variables Assets and Revenues to normalize the distribution of skewed variables and improving model fit. The model fitted is described in Equation (1).

\[\begin{equation} \log(MarketCap) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 EconomicSector + \beta_2 Profits + \beta_3 log(Assets) + \beta_4 log(Revenue) \tag{1} \end{equation}\]


Results


Linear model for Fortune 2023 dataset

Linear model results for 2023 year as presented in the Table 4 below indicate that overall chosen predictors significantly affect the Market Value. The model explains approximately 44.93 % of the variance in log of MarketCap, and an adjusted R-squared 0.4423 suggesting a moderate fit. F-statistic is 63.78 and small p.value of less than 0.001 confirm that the linear model is statistically significant. Among the predictors, EconomicSector4 (quaternary) has the strongest positive relationship with the Market Value, with a coefficient of 0.8068 and statistically significant p.value of < 0.001. EconomicSector also has strong positive relationship with a coefficient of 0.4387 and is statistically significant p.value of 0.0083. While EconomicSector3 has a negative coefficient of -0.1480 and is not statistically significant. log Assets and log Revenues act as significant predictors with coefficients of 0.4000 and 0.3921 respectively and both have statistically significant p.value of < 0.001. While Profits appeared to be not a strong predictor of Market Value with a coefficient nearly zero. The 97 % confidence intervals suggest reliability of the estimated coefficients.

Checked assumptions for the Fortune 2023 model

We have checked assumptions of linear model of year 2023, namely - linearity, independence, normality and equal variance. As can be seen in Figure 9, linearity (Residuals vs Fitted values) is likely satisfied as residuals look randomly scattered. Independence ( Residuals by Observation Order) is also likely satisfied since the residuals look randomly scattered with no trends in particular. Normality ( QQ plot of Residuals) is on the contrary, not likely to be satisfied, since the residuals are not normally distributed due to outliers near the left tail. Equal variance (Absolute Residuals vs Fitted Values) is also not likely to be satisfied as graph clearly suggests heteroscedasticity.


Figure 9: Linear model assumptions for 2023

Predicted value

Assuming the model is trustworthy we want to calculate the expected market value of a company in the quaternary sector with 100,000 employees, revenue of 100 000 USD millions, a loss of 5000 USD millions and assets of 50 000 USD millions. The following prediction is based on 90% prediction intervals. As a result, the predicted market value of such company is around 32 710 USD millions, within 90% prediction interval that true value will fall between 5010 and 213 557 USD millions. Prediction interval suggests much broader range, which can be due to a higher uncertainty and variability related to a number of predictors. See Table 6

Discussion and Conclusions

Linear model demonstrated reasonable significance with adjusted R-squared values of 0.4423 for 2023 year and 0.4728 for 2024 year. This suggests that the model explains approximately 44% and 47% of the variance in the log of MarketCap for 2023 and 2024 years respectfully.

The most significant predictors of the Market Value appeared Economic Sector ( 4 and 2 in particular) along with log of Assets and Revenue for both years. Interestingly, while Profits highly correlated with Market Value as was seen in Figure 4, this predictor appeared as not significant in the linear model. We can assume that this may be explained by the multicollinearity with other financial metrics or model’s failure to capture the relationship between Profits and Market Value relative to other predictors.

Predicted estimate of Market Value of a company with certain parameters had been provided with a very broad prediction interval. This suggests significant uncertainty that can be connected to variability of predictors or that Market Value can be influenced by other predictors, that have not been captured by the linear model. Overall, given the limitations of fitted model, we recommend to explore other factors and their associations with the Market Value to fit a better model with more precise predictions.
